espn-603993.headline: Contepomi back in Dublin with a side that loses by a score
beats: Felipe Contepomi, once a Leinster star, brings Argentina to the Aviva Stadium. Since beating Wales 35–21 in July, his side have lost to England by seven, South Africa by seven and Australia by six, then drew the rematch with Australia 28–28.
The last meeting, in November 2024, went to Ireland 22–19. That is roughly the margin Argentina have been living on ever since.
Ireland's last game was a 40–21 loss at Eden Park in July. They are without both Jack Conan and Caelan Doris at No. 8.
An Argentina win drops Ireland to fourth in the world, below France. After a run of close calls, this would be the narrow margin going the other way.

espn-603994.headline: Six uncapped Boks on tour, none of them for Italy
beats: Rassie Erasmus brought six uncapped players to Europe and picked none of them to face a side that lost all three of its July games. Nick Mallett traces the choice to August's 16–33 home defeat by New Zealand, which he put down to "a lack of cohesion in the team."

Italy conceded 47 and then 57 on consecutive Saturdays in July, and Gonzalo Quesada now has an injury crisis on top. South Africa lost their last game as well, 38–42 in Australia, despite scoring six tries.
The Springboks' only defeat to Italy came in Florence in 2016. Repeat it in Turin and New Zealand take first place in the world rankings.

Salmaan Moerat, missing since the start of the campaign with neck and toe injuries, is the only one of the 23 yet to play for South Africa this year. France away comes six days later, so Italy get the side built for France.

espn-603995.headline: 121 years of trying, and New Zealand pack the full side
beats: Scotland have never beaten New Zealand in 33 attempts. Mike Blair, once Scotland's captain and now a New Zealand assistant, recalls the days the Scots got a second-string side. This time New Zealand come "fully loaded", with a record they call real motivation.
The tour has already brought grief. Logan Cadwallader, the All Blacks' head of security for a decade, died at their team hotel in Edinburgh, and the squad say they are heartbroken.

Last November at Murrayfield it finished 17–25, and Blair concedes the last four meetings have been close. Scotland score freely and concede the same way: 47–38 against Argentina, 42 let in against South Africa.
New Zealand lost three in a row to South Africa, then put 50 and 43 on Australia. Win, and Scotland go above England to fifth in the world, which would be the smaller of the two things they changed.

espn-603996.headline: A point split them last year. A point splits them now
beats: Wales beat Japan 24–23 in Cardiff on 15 November 2025. They meet again with Wales ninth in the Nations Championship on five points and Japan one behind in tenth.

Wales have not played since a 0–43 loss to South Africa on 18 July, which followed a 21–35 defeat by Argentina. Japan's last outing was a 28–34 loss to Fiji on 24 October, in which they scored four tries.

Defence is where Wales are looking. Across three July games they missed more than 100 tackles and conceded 15 tries. Their defence coach, Peter Murchie, joined from Kobelco Kobe Steelers, so he knows something of the players he is trying to stop. He wants Wales tougher to break down.
A Japan win by any margin puts them above Wales and Italy in the world rankings. Neither side gets an easy week afterwards: Wales host New Zealand on 14 November, and Japan go to England.

espn-603997.headline: France insist South Africa are next week's problem
beats: Mickael Guillard says France have not discussed South Africa, who come next. “We’re focused on Fiji,” he said. Fabien Galthié has added five players ahead of the South Africa game all the same.
Fiji are last of twelve without a point, and conceded 73 to England in July. They also won 34–28 in Tokyo on 24 October, and ten of that side flew straight on to camp in Lyon.
France won the last meeting 34–21 at home in November 2025. Lose by 15 or fewer here and they drop to fifth in the world, below England, the side they beat 48–46 in March.
Guillard calls his club team-mate Jiuta Wainiqolo “a phenomenon”. South Africa can wait a week. Wainiqolo cannot.

espn-603998.headline: England lose their nine and perhaps their ten as well
beats: Alex Mitchell is out of the whole Nations Championship with his fourth hamstring injury of the year. Archie McParland, 21 and uncapped, hurt a calf in the training camp, so Ben Spencer and Harry Randall are called up behind Jack van Poortvliet, who started all three summer Tests.
Fly-half is no safer. Fin Smith started at 10 in all three July Tests and is nursing a calf, with Marcus Smith and George Ford competing to deputise.
Australia beat South Africa 42–38, then conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in the following month. Win at Allianz Stadium and they go up to fifth in the world, with England dropping to seventh.

England won last November's meeting 25–7. Australia arrive amid a pay stalemate between Rugby Australia and the players' union. England's problems are at nine and ten. Australia's are at the negotiating table.

espn-603999.headline: Win in Saint-Denis and France make New Zealand No.1
beats: South Africa have been world No.1 since 31 August. Beat them at the Stade de France and New Zealand go top, with France up to third above Ireland.

When they met in November 2025, France were at home and lost 17–32. Since then the scoring has loosened. South Africa conceded 42 in Australia in September, and France put 42 on both Australia and Japan in July.

Steven Kitshoff calls France the biggest "must-win" hurdle on the way to a final spot. Stephen Donald, who backs New Zealand to reach that final ahead of South Africa, thinks this is where they could come unstuck.
Rassie Erasmus picked a full-strength side for Italy, with France and Ireland to follow. Ireland, away, comes a week after this, so any lesson from Saint-Denis has to sink in quickly.

espn-604000.headline: Italy's newest No 10 has ten Argentina caps
beats: Domingo Miotti's last Test for Argentina was on 9 July 2022. The Montpellier flyhalf, 30, qualifies through an Italian grandfather and is now in Gonzalo Quesada's 33-man squad, one of four No 10 options alongside Paolo Garbisi, Tommaso Allan and Giacomo Da Re.
Italy could use a fresh idea. They lost all three Nations Championship games in July, conceding 47 in New Zealand and 57 in Australia. South Africa come to Turin first.
Argentina arrive by way of Dublin, where Felipe Contepomi takes them to face Ireland. Their last Test was a 28–28 draw with Australia, which was at least not a loss.
Win and Italy climb above Wales and Fiji. Fiji are the side Italy host a week later, and the only one below them on the log, so Miotti's new team could do with his old one being polite.

espn-604001.headline: Wales's best day against them in Cardiff ended 26–52
beats: Last November in Cardiff, Rogers became the first player since 2004 to score a hat-trick against New Zealand, and Wales put up their most points against them in Cardiff. Reuters still filed it as New Zealand's 34th consecutive win over Wales.

Scoring is not the worry. Wales missed more than 100 tackles and conceded 15 tries across three July games, the last a 43–0 in South Africa, and defence coach Peter Murchie wants a vast improvement. New Zealand have scored seven tries in each of their last two Tests.
Win and Wales climb to ninth in the world. New Zealand have more riding on it, level on points with South Africa at the top of the Nations Championship.
Wales host Australia a week later. Rogers's hat-trick says points are possible against this side; the streak says points were never the problem.

espn-604002.headline: Italy beat England in March. Japan rank below Italy.
beats: England have sat fifth in the world since July. Japan are 12th, down from ninth in October. Neither fact stopped Italy beating England 23–18 in March, or France putting 48 on them a week later.

England are without Alex Mitchell for the whole Nations Championship after his fourth hamstring injury of the year, and Fin Smith has been nursing a calf. Jack van Poortvliet was expected to take the scrum-half shirt against Australia.
Japan beat Fiji 20–15 in September and lost to them 34–28 in October. A Japan win here lifts them to ninth and drops England to seventh, below Scotland and Australia.
England host New Zealand next, which is no week to be explaining seventh.

espn-604003.headline: Ireland have nothing to gain and a place to lose
beats: Ireland can win by any margin and stay exactly third in the world. Every other result costs them a place. Fiji, ninth, are the only side here with anything to collect.

Fiji sit bottom of the Nations Championship, pointless after three games and 96 in the red. Most of that came in one afternoon, 8–73 at home to England. They did win their last Test, 34–28 away to Japan in October.

This is the middle of Ireland's three home games, after Argentina and before South Africa. Sixth on 10 points, level with Scotland, Farrell's side need all three, and three wins would almost certainly put them in a final against New Zealand or South Africa.

The second strings meet in Cork on 20 November, where Joey Carbery is pushing for a recall against Fiji A. South Africa arrive in Dublin the next day, which is the game Ireland would rather be thinking about.

espn-604004.headline: Australia conceded 93 in a fortnight and called Beale
beats: New Zealand put 50 and 43 past Australia in October. Les Kiss's answer for the tour includes Kurtley Beale, 37, recalled with a World Cup place in view: "He’s in there to perform".
Scotland score freely and concede the same way: 50–40 against France in March, 47–38 away to Argentina in July. It is not the profile of a side built to make a leaky defence pay with patience.

Scotland are without flanker Jamie Ritchie and prop Elliot Millar Mills, both hurt playing for their clubs. They sit sixth in the world, one place above Australia, and an Australian win at Murrayfield swaps them.
Australia's Nations Championship points difference is still better than Scotland's. The 93 came in friendlies, which is one way to keep them off the table.
